streetview.pano_ids_note: the two Google panoramas (2026-04, 42-44 m) that the sight-line test over the LiDAR finds seeing most of the west and south faces (MGAo: S 70%, W 67%, SW 54%; W9y5: W 55%); the other 18 Google panoramas within 80 m see under 2% of the faces turned to them, behind trees and neighbours
streetview.camera_fixes_note: MGAo's camera fitted to its tower view's own edges against the LiDAR's (round 2, 2026-10-27): 20 floor bands on the shaft's brick faces either side of the slot (columns 545-775, rows 66-339) as the floors at 25.88, 28.75, 31.62 and 34.50 m, the heights where the wall returns peak, on the faces' lines fitted to the LiDAR's wall returns (rms 0.03-0.08 m); the brick's left edge (columns 515-517) on the west corner (14.3, -4.2) and the slot's middle (column 681) on the slot's corner (12.49, -8.48); and the top of the entrance canopy's red tiles (row 960 at columns 300-390) on the LiDAR's canopy roof at 8.76 m. The camera stands 1.36 m west and 1.18 m south of the recorded one (1.8 m; 40.0 m from the frame's centre, 38.3 m recorded) and the photograph looks 5.56 deg lower than its cut says (the third number, std 0.36 deg); residuals: the bands -23.6 to +13.1 px, the corners and the canopy within 2.8 px, rms 10.4 px over 27 (80 px at the recorded camera). Without a pitch the best fit moves the camera 2.8 m nearer and leaves the canopy 98 px off (rms 33.8 px): a point near the camera's height does not move when the camera does. A pitch of that size is what the panorama's own roll gives: it records a roll of -4.16 deg and a tilt of 0.8 deg (the car on the street's cross-slope), which tools/streetview_collect.py does not apply when it cuts the views, and the tower view looks 71 deg off the car's heading, where that roll alone is 3.9 deg of pitch. W9y5's camera is not fitted: its views show the tower only in patches through leaves, with no edge or roof corner. Only the camera the views are drawn from moves and turns; they are cut from the panorama as before
